name: Romulus Labs Content Publisher for Rankwise
author: romerogers

sections.description:
This plugin connects a WordPress site to Rankwise, a service that helps a site get found and cited by AI answer engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini.

This plugin is the WordPress end of that service. It needs a Rankwise account: without one it does nothing and sends nothing.

Once you connect the site, you can:

  • Publish articles. Articles you approve in Rankwise arrive as WordPress posts or pages, with their title, excerpt, slug, categories, tags and hero image. Re-publishing an article updates the same post instead of creating a duplicate. Elementor sites can have the Elementor edit flags set for them.
  • Apply AI-visibility fixes (optional, off by default). Rankwise proposes fixes for your pages, such as structured data (JSON-LD), head tags, robots.txt lines and an llms.txt file. If you switch this on and paste your delivery secret, the plugin downloads the fixes you approved, checks their signature, and adds them when pages are served. If anything fails, your site renders exactly as it did. Not available yet: Rankwise has not switched on fix delivery for accounts, so today Rankwise shows you each proposed fix and its exact change, and this setting has nothing to download until delivery opens.
  • Ping IndexNow when you publish (optional, off by default). Sends the URL of a post you publish or update to IndexNow, so Bing, Yandex and other participating engines re-crawl it sooner.
  • Report AI-crawler visits (optional, off by default). Counts visits from AI crawlers such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot and sends Rankwise a daily summary, so you can see whether the AI engines are actually reaching your pages.

Nothing is sent anywhere when you install or activate the plugin. The plugin shows no ads, adds no links or credits to your public site, and has no locked or paid features of its own: every feature in the plugin works for every connected account.

How publishing is secured

Each connected site gets its own API key and shared secret. Every request Rankwise sends to your site is signed with an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the exact request body, and the plugin refuses any request whose key or signature does not match. Only the two routes the plugin registers (rankwise/v1/articles and rankwise/v1/media) accept these requests, and the media route accepts image files only.

External services

This plugin connects to services outside your WordPress site. Here is each one, what it is used for, what is sent, and when.

Rankwise (tryrankwise.com)

Rankwise is the service this plugin belongs to, run by the company named on the Rankwise legal notice.

  • When you click Connect with Rankwise: your browser opens https://tryrankwise.com/dashboard/integrations/connect/wordpress with this site’s address, the address of the plugin screen to return to, and a one-time security code. Rankwise sends your browser back to the plugin screen with a connect token, and the plugin then connects as described in the next point.
  • When you connect the site (with Connect with Rankwise, or by pasting a connect token and pressing Connect Site): the token, this site’s address, the site title, a random site ID created by the plugin, your WordPress user ID and email address, the plugin version, and whether Elementor is active are sent to https://tryrankwise.com/api/wordpress/sites. Rankwise returns the API key and shared secret the site uses from then on.
  • When you press Test Connection: a request with no plugin data is sent to the same address to check it can be reached.
  • When you disconnect: a signed request with an empty body tells Rankwise to forget the connection.
  • When Rankwise publishes to your site: Rankwise calls your site, not the other way round. The plugin replies with the new post ID, its URL and its status.
  • Only if you switch on AI-visibility fixes: when a page is served, at most once every five minutes, the plugin requests your fixes from https://tryrankwise.com/api/remediation/bundle, sending only your site’s domain name.
  • Only if you switch on AI-crawler reports and the site is connected: once a day, the plugin sends https://tryrankwise.com/api/integrations/crawler-telemetry a summary of AI-crawler visits: the crawler name, the date, the number of visits and the most visited paths. Visits by people are never counted, and no IP addresses, cookies or personal data are recorded or sent.
  • Updates: this copy of the plugin is updated through WordPress.org, not through Rankwise.

Like every request WordPress makes, each of these carries WordPress’s standard user agent, which includes your WordPress version and site address.

Rankwise terms of service and privacy policy.

IndexNow (api.indexnow.org)

IndexNow is an open protocol that lets a site tell participating search engines (including Bing and Yandex) that a URL has changed.

  • Only if you switch on IndexNow: when you publish or update a public post, its URL, your site’s host name and your site’s IndexNow key are sent to https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow. The plugin also serves the key as a small text file at /<key>.txt on your site, which is how IndexNow checks that you own the site.

IndexNow terms of use, which include its privacy provisions, and documentation.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins, then Add New, by searching for “Rankwise”, or upload the zip file.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. In WordPress, open Rankwise Publisher in the admin menu and click Connect with Rankwise. Sign in to Rankwise, confirm the site, and you come back connected.
  4. Or, without leaving WordPress: in Rankwise, open Dashboard, then Integrations, choose WordPress and generate a connect token (it expires after 30 minutes), then paste it into Rankwise Publisher and press Connect Site.
  5. Optional: in the same screen, switch on any of the AI-visibility features you want and press Save settings.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Rankwise account?

Yes. The plugin is the WordPress side of the Rankwise service. Without a connected account it does nothing and contacts no one.

Does the plugin send anything when I install or activate it?

No. Nothing leaves your site until you connect it to Rankwise or switch on one of the optional features.

Will Rankwise overwrite posts I wrote myself?

No. The plugin only updates posts it created for a Rankwise article, which it recognises by a hidden article ID stored with the post.

Does the plugin add a “Powered by” link or any credit to my site?

No. Nothing is added to your public pages except the AI-visibility fixes you approved and switched on yourself.

What happens if Rankwise is unreachable?

Your site keeps working. The optional features fail open: if a fix bundle cannot be fetched or its signature does not match, nothing is applied, and a crawler report that cannot be sent is kept and retried the next day.

How do I remove everything the plugin stored?

Delete the plugin from the Plugins screen. Its settings, its stored crawler counts and its scheduled task are removed. Posts and images it published stay, because they are your content.

Can I point the plugin at a test server?

Yes, for development. Define RANKWISE_PUBLISHER_REMOTE_URL in wp-config.php, or use the rankwise_publisher_remote_url filter.
sections.changelog:
0.7.0

  • New: publish into a custom post type you choose in Rankwise.
  • New: the author name set in Rankwise picks the matching site user.
  • Fixed: tags and categories set in Rankwise now reach the post.

0.6.0

  • New: Connect with Rankwise. One click from the plugin screen connects the site, with no token to copy.
  • Articles from Rankwise now carry Article and FAQ structured data, printed in the page head.

0.5.0

  • Prepared for WordPress.org: GPL license header, readme and a full External services section.
  • IndexNow pings and AI-crawler reports are now off until you switch them on.
  • Removed the anonymous activation ping.
  • The settings screen now says what is sent when you connect the site.
  • The media route accepts image files only.
  • AI-visibility fixes never emit event-handler attributes, and well-known files are only served as plain text, Markdown, JSON or XML.
  • Fixed a spurious “Connect token is required” error when disconnecting.
  • Deleting the plugin now removes its settings and scheduled task.

0.4.0

  • Settings screen for AI-visibility fixes, IndexNow and AI-crawler reports.

0.3.0

  • AI-visibility fixes applied server-side: structured data, head tags, robots.txt lines and well-known files.
